parsed.explanation: The flagship trans-specific criminal offence (imitating opposite sex) was struck down in 2022, but the record shows dress-code policing and official discrimination persisting through 2023, with no legislative repeal confirmed, no LGBTQ association, and an ombudsman without force. Article 193's enforced seven-year penalty for conduct read under birth-sex status reaches a trans visitor in (or perceived to be in) a same-sex relationship; public-morality prosecutions are documented. Gender segregation, strict dress codes, film/content censorship, and foreign-national HIV deportation compound exposure. The 2017 two-week detention for 'looking too feminine' shows custody is reachable. No violence baseline, no remedy that operates, thin data overall resolves toward the structural risks these facts imply.

entry_documents.exposure: No implemented entry-screening regime documented (2013 subregional 'testing' proposal disavowed). Foreign nationals found HIV-positive are deported — a documented traveller-facing exclusion. Residents cannot change documents, a resident gap only.
entry_documents.protection: No documented entry denial or document-based screening of transgender visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Any health screening or document check at the border could interact with the HIV deportation rule or presentation mismatch.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2017 detention for two weeks of a person for 'looking too feminine'; Article 193 enforced with up to seven years' imprisonment reaches a visitor read as same-sex under birth-sex status; post-2022 official discrimination documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2022 Constitutional Court invalidation removed the cross-dressing offence's criminal exposure on paper.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Dress-code policing outlasted the ruling; enforcement encounters after 2022 are undocumented, so residual arrest risk is real but unsized.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Gender segregation and enforced dress codes documented nationally (university gender-segregation decisions; subregional overview), constraining gendered spaces for outed visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No subnational variation exists to mitigate or worsen; no facility protections documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Segregation regimes push any presentation mismatch into official view, feeding policing and service denial.

care_services.exposure: HIV-positive foreign nationals deported while citizens receive care; no trans-specific care access documented; official discrimination in services persisted in 2023.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking can trigger disclosure with deportation as the documented consequence; emergency or minor-related care is not covered anywhere in the record.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Public morality laws strictly enforced with documented LGBTQ prosecutions; censorship (films, LGBTQI+ legal information blocked), commerce-ministry crackdown on LGBTQ symbols, no open LGBTQ legislators — sustained official threat-framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional Court ruling signals one working judicial check.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Censorship removes legal information a visitor might use, worsening outcomes after any stop.

minors_guardians.exposure: No youth-specific or minor-specific provisions documented; a trans parent travelling with a minor faces the same morality policing and segregation, with no documented custody or guardianship rule either way.
minors_guardians.interaction: Unknown — the record does not address children accompanying gender-nonconforming visitors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police targeting of gender-nonconforming presentation documented (2017 arrest; persistence after 2022); gender-based violence and arbitrary detention cited in 2023 reporting. No trans-specific violence rate or homicide baseline present.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absent a functioning remedy, a street or policing encounter has no corrective path.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No LGBTQ association exists (2007 application unanswered); ombudsman urged repeal that may not have happened; discrimination by officials persisted a year after the ruling; censorship blocks advocacy and legal information.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2022 Constitutional Court ruling invalidated the cross-dressing offence; national legal library corroborates.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Judicial relief operated once but did not translate into legislative repeal, police practice change, or civil-society recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this dossier: Karthovia's exposure is stops and short releases with no credible imprisonment. Here an enforced seven-year sodomy statute reaches a trans visitor read under birth-sex status, morality prosecutions are documented, and no effective remedy or civil society exists.

Closest fit. Ostravia combines a cross-dressing statute, birth-sex housing and slow remedies; this dossier's statute was struck down (better) but retains an enforced relationship-based imprisonment exposure, active censorship and zero advocacy infrastructure (worse), so roughly level.

Higher than this anchor: Belvane documents interrogation-centre torture, years-long sentences and closed judicial review. Nothing in this dossier shows custodial torture, fabricated confessions, or execution pathways — imprisonment is reachable but not routine or abusive-custody documented.

parsed.synthesis: The 2022 ruling is the record's single genuine protection, and it removes the clearest trans-specific criminal charge — but it is partial: no confirmed legislative repeal, dress-code policing and official discrimination documented a year later, and no organisation, media channel, or ombudsman able to convert the ruling into relief. Against that, an enforced Article 193 plus strict public-morality policing means an outed visitor — particularly one read as having a partner — faces credible imprisonment, while everyday exposure (segregated spaces, dress codes, censorship, HIV deportation) is continuous. Absence of violence statistics leaves the violence axis unresolved, not safe; the structural picture justifies a High Risk reading rather than Elevated.
